messages.content: My daughter gave me her old Google Pixel when she got a new phone. It works fine but I can't read anything without my glasses and I always forget where I put them. Is there a way to make the letters on the screen bigger?

Yes. You can make the writing larger in Settings. It takes about a minute.

1. Open the **Settings** app.
2. Tap the search bar at the top of Settings.
3. Type **Font size**.
4. Tap **Font size** in the results.
5. Move the slider toward the larger end until the text is easy to read.

The change happens right away. A few apps ignore this setting, so text in those apps may stay the same size.

If you can't find **Font size**, tell me what you see after searching and I'll help you find it.

sources.title: Android Accessibility Help: Change text & display settings

messages.content: My grandson is helping me with my phone over the phone and he keeps saying send me a screenshot so he can see what I see. I don't know what that is or how to do it.

A screenshot is a picture of exactly what's on your screen, so your grandson can see it too. The buttons to take one depend on your phone.

messages.content: How do I connect my Windows 11 laptop to Wi-Fi?

Here's how. Have your Wi-Fi password ready. This takes about two minutes.

1. On the taskbar at the bottom right of the screen, click the **network, sound, or battery icons**. A small panel opens.
2. Next to the Wi-Fi button, click the **arrow** for **Manage Wi-Fi connections**.
3. Click the name of your network.
4. Click **Connect**.
5. Type your Wi-Fi password.
6. Click **Next**.

When it's done, try opening a website to check that it works.

If you don't see your network in the list, click **Refresh network list** in the lower right of the panel and look again.

sources.title: Microsoft Support: Connect to a Wi-Fi network in Windows

messages.content: How do I attach a photo to an email in the Gmail app on my Android phone?

Here's how. It takes about a minute.

1. Open the **Gmail** app.
2. Tap **Compose** at the bottom right to start a new email.
3. Tap the **Attach** icon at the top right. It looks like a **paperclip**.
4. Choose where the photo is, such as **Photos**.
5. Tap the photo you want. You can pick up to five photos at once.

Then add the email address and your message as usual, and send it.

If you added the wrong photo, tap the close icon (**X**) next to its name to remove it. Files over 25 MB are added as a Google Drive link instead.

sources.title: Gmail Help: Send attachments with your Gmail message (Android)

messages.content: I got a text about a package, is it real?
Let's check it together. **What does the text ask you to do?** For example, does it have a link to click, or ask you to pay a fee or update your address?
It has a link and says I need to pay $1.99 for redelivery.

Thanks. A small fee plus a link is a very common sign of a scam, even when you really are expecting a package. Please **don't click the link**. It usually leads to a fake website that looks real and asks for your personal or card information.

Instead:

1. **Don't click** the link or reply.
2. Check on your package using the website or app of the **store where you bought it**. Go there directly, not through the text.
3. **Report the text.** Use your phone's **junk** or **spam** reporting option if you see one, or forward the text to **7726**. You can also report it at **ReportFraud.ftc.gov**.
4. Then delete it.

If you already clicked and typed in your card number, call your bank right away using the number on the back of your card.

sources.title: FTC Consumer Alert: Think that text message is from USPS? It could be a scam

messages.content: There's a number from out of state that calls me three or four times a day. When I answer nobody's there. My neighbor said I should block it but I don't know how. I have an iPhone 11.

Your neighbor is right: blocking it will stop those calls from ringing. You can do it from your list of recent calls in less than a minute.

1. Open the **Phone** app.
2. Tap **Recents**.
3. Find the number and tap it. (If you see a small **"i"** in a circle next to the number, tap that instead.)
4. Scroll down and tap **Block Caller**.
5. If a message asks you to confirm, tap **Block Contact**.

After that, calls from that number won't ring your phone, and the caller won't be told they're blocked. If they leave a voicemail, it's saved, but you won't get a notification.

sources.title: Apple Support: Block phone numbers, contacts, and emails on your iPhone or iPad

messages.content: how can my daughter see where I am
That's a nice way to give her peace of mind. Is your phone an **iPhone** or an **Android** phone? And does your daughter have an iPhone or Android?
We both have iPhones

Great. Since you both have iPhones, you can do this in the **Find My** app. It takes about two minutes. You and your daughter both need iPhones with a recent software update.

1. Open the **Find My** app.
2. Tap **Me** at the bottom, and make sure **Share My Location** is turned on.
3. Tap **People** at the bottom.
4. Tap the **Add** button (a plus sign), then tap **Share My Location**.
5. Type your daughter's name and tap it when it appears.
6. Tap **Send**.
7. Choose how long to share, such as **one hour**, **until the end of the day**, or **indefinitely**. Some versions also let you pick a custom time.

Your daughter can then see where you are in her Find My app.

Only share your location with people you trust.

messages.content: how do I get rid of an app
Sure. Is your phone an **iPhone** or an **Android** phone?
iphone

Thanks.

Here's how. It takes a few seconds.

1. Find the app on your Home Screen.
2. **Press and hold** the app's icon until a menu appears.
3. Tap **Remove App**.
4. Tap **Delete App**.
5. Tap **Delete** to confirm.

If the icons start to jiggle instead of showing a menu:
1. Tap the **minus** sign in the app's upper-left corner.
2. Tap **Delete App**.
3. Tap **Delete**.
4. Tap **Done** at the top of the screen.

Deleting an app also removes its data from your phone. If you might want it later, you can download it again from the App Store.

Deleting an app does **not** cancel any paid subscriptions inside it. If you pay for the app every month, cancel the subscription first.

messages.content: I met a man online three months ago. He says he loves me, he works on an oil rig overseas, and now he needs $2,000 for a plane ticket to come see me. Should I send it?

I'm glad you asked before sending anything. Please **don't send the money**. What you're describing matches a very common scam called a **romance scam**.

**Warning signs:**
- The person can't meet in person, often saying they work far away, like on an **oil rig** or in the military.
- Strong feelings grow quickly through lots of messages.
- Now there's a **need for money**, like travel costs or an emergency.

**What to do:**
1. **Don't send money or gift cards** to someone you haven't met in person.
2. **Talk to a friend or family member** you trust. People close to you can often spot things that are hard to see from the inside.
3. You can **search his photo** online to see if it appears under other names. I can show you how.
4. If it's a scam, stop contact and report it at **ReportFraud.ftc.gov** and to the website or app where you met.

If you've already sent money, contact your bank or the payment company right away and ask for a refund.

sources.title: FTC Consumer Advice: What To Know About Romance Scams

messages.content: My iPhone only vibrates when someone calls. It doesn't ring. How do I fix that?

Your iPhone is probably in **Silent mode**. Here's how to check.

**If your iPhone has a small switch on the side** (above the volume buttons):
1. Look at the switch. If you see **orange**, Silent mode is on.
2. Flip the switch so the orange no longer shows.

**If your iPhone has an Action button instead** (iPhone 15 Pro and newer):
1. **Press and hold** the **Action button** until you see Silent mode turn off at the top of the screen. By default, this button turns Silent mode on and off. If it's been set to do something else, tell me and we'll check another way.

Once Silent mode is off, your phone will ring again. If it's still too quiet, press the **volume up** button while you're on the Home Screen.

sources.title: Apple Support: Use the volume buttons, side button, and other controls on your iPhone

messages.content: 我那個認識三十年的老同學，今天突然在LINE上跟我說他住院缺錢，要我先轉三萬給他，說他不方便講電話。我很想幫他，但覺得怪怪的。

messages.content: How do I make the text bigger on my iPhone? Everything is too small to read.

You can make the text bigger in Settings. It takes about a minute, and you can change it back anytime.

1. Open the **Settings** app. Its icon is a gray gear.
2. Tap **Display & Brightness**.
3. Tap **Text Size**.
4. Drag the slider at the bottom of the screen to the right.

The sample text changes as you drag, so you can stop when it's easy to read.

If you need it even bigger, go to **Settings**, then **Accessibility**, then **Display & Text Size**, then **Larger Text**, and drag that slider. Very large text can make some buttons harder to tap, so slide it back a little if that happens.
I made it really big and now some of the buttons are cut off and hard to tap.

That can happen when the text is set very large. Let's make it a little smaller so the buttons fit again.

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Display & Brightness**.
3. Tap **Text Size**.
4. Drag the slider **one step to the left**.
5. Go back to the app and check the buttons.

If you made the text bigger with **Larger Text** instead, the slider is in **Settings**, then **Accessibility**, then **Display & Text Size**, then **Larger Text**.

Repeat until the buttons fit on the screen and the text is still easy for you to read.

sources.title: Apple Support: Change the font size on your iPhone, iPad, and iPod touch

messages.content: I'm staying at my daughter's house this weekend. She wrote the Wi-Fi name and password on a card for me. The network is called SmithHome. I have an iPhone 13 with the latest update. How do I get my phone on her internet?

Here's how to connect your iPhone to SmithHome. Keep the card with the password nearby. This takes about two minutes.

1. Open the **Settings** app. Its icon is a gray gear.
2. Tap **Wi-Fi** near the top.
3. Make sure the switch next to **Wi-Fi** is on (green).
4. Wait a moment for a list of networks to appear. Tap **SmithHome**.
5. Type the password from the card. Capital and small letters must match exactly.
6. Tap **Join**.

When you're connected, you'll see a blue checkmark next to **SmithHome**, and a Wi-Fi symbol (it looks like a fan) at the top of your screen.

If it says the password is incorrect, tap **SmithHome** again and retype it slowly. If you don't see SmithHome in the list, move closer to the internet box in her home and check again.
I don't see SmithHome in the list at all.

Let's check a few things. Try them in order, and stop as soon as **SmithHome** appears in the list.

1. **Check the exact name.** Ask your daughter to check the network name. It might be slightly different, like **SmithHome-5G**.
2. **Ask whether other phones work.** Ask your daughter whether other phones in the house can connect.
3. **Check the internet box.** Make sure the router is plugged in and its lights are on.
4. **Move closer** to the router, then look at the list again.
5. **Check Airplane Mode.** In **Settings**, make sure **Airplane Mode** is turned off.
6. **Check the Wi-Fi switch.** If it looks gray and you can't tap it, restart your iPhone.
7. **Restart the router.** Unplug the router and the modem, then plug them back in. Ask your daughter first, because this turns off the internet for everyone in the house for a few minutes.

If SmithHome still doesn't show up, tell me which network names you do see.

sources.title: Apple Support: Connect to Wi-Fi on your iPhone or iPad
Apple Support: If you can't connect to Wi-Fi on your iPhone or iPad

messages.content: I got an email from my pastor asking me to buy five $100 gift cards for church members and send him the numbers on the back. He said he's in a meeting and can't talk. Should I do it?

Please **don't buy the gift cards**. This is a common scam. Real businesses, government agencies, and people you know don't ask to be paid with gift card numbers, and once you share the numbers, the money is very hard to get back.

Here's what to do:

1. **Don't reply** to the email.
2. **Call your pastor** using a phone number you already have, or call the church office, and ask if he really sent it.
3. If it's fake, you can report it at **ReportFraud.ftc.gov**.

**If you already bought cards and shared the numbers:**
- Call the **gift card company** right away and ask for your money back. Sometimes they can freeze what's left on the card.
- Keep the cards and the store receipt.
- Report it at **ReportFraud.ftc.gov**.
Oh no. I already bought two $100 cards this morning and emailed him the numbers before I saw this.

I'm sorry this happened. This scam fools a lot of careful people. Acting quickly gives you the best chance of getting money back.

1. **Contact the gift card company right away.** Tell them the cards were used in a scam and ask for your money back. Sometimes they can freeze money that hasn't been spent yet. The FTC's gift card scam page lists contact information for major gift card companies.
2. **Keep the cards and the store receipt**, and take a photo of both. You'll need them when you report it.
3. **Report the scam** at **ReportFraud.ftc.gov**.
4. **Don't reply** to the email, and don't buy more cards, even if you're asked again.
5. **Tell your church office**, so they can warn other members, and let your pastor know his email may have been hacked.

Do you have the cards and the receipt with you? If so, we can look at step 1 together.

sources.title: FTC Consumer Advice: Avoiding and Reporting Gift Card Scams
